newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toho Mutual's problem loans at 59.8 billion yen.
newsitem.headline: Toho Mutual's problem loans at 59.8 billion yen.

text.p: Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co said on Tuesday that its problem loans totalled 59.8 billion yen at the end of March, 1997, down from 66.65 billion yen a year earlier.
Problem loans accounted for four percent of its total loans outstanding at the end of March, unchanged from a year earlier, the insurer said in a statement.
The life insurer earlier announced that its premium income fell to 599.53 billion yen in 1996/97 ended March 31 from 747.37 billion a year earlier.
It posted a parent current profit of 6.76 billion yen in the last business year against 8.52 billion yen a year earlier.

Since Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, a medium-sized insurer, was ordered to halt operations in April -- the first failure of a Japanese life insurer in the postwar period -- rumours have circulated in the industry that other small and medium-sized insurers are also in trouble.
Last month, Toho Mutual said its restructuring efforts were having a positive effect and that it would be able to post a current profit for 1996/97 ended March 31.
The company said that its unrealised profit on stockholdings fell to 20.69 billion yen at the end of March from 63.35 billion yen in the same period a year earlier.
Its unrealised profits on all marketable securities holdings fell to 16.01 billion yen from 61.46 billion yen.
A company executive said that unrealised profits on its shareholdings would fall to zero if the key Nikkei stock average declines to somewhere between 17,000 and 17,500.
